analysis:
This pass examined documentation-only changes; no provider source was supplied.

hardware-support.md: head units 888-1293 hold unchanged context. The changed range is head 451-488, the selected-model recovery description, which is visible only in the file_changes excerpt and was not in these units.

model-autopilot.md:
- Head 158: the adoption end conditions now include release by selected-model recovery after the adoption's hold ends.
- Head 182-219 describe recovery. Recovery re-queues selected models that an operation unloaded and loads them with allowEviction:false. It may unload an unheld adopted slot that meets the victim rules: min_dwell_seconds, no unexpired per-model lease, and idle for the longer of 2 min and min_idle_seconds. It never evicts the ordinary selection, Autopilot pins, held slots or advertised models that a request could reload. It counts as busy 'preload'. An add-on hold pauses it and cancels an attempt in progress (enterAddonHold).
- Adoption release: 10 minutes after the later of hold expiry and the start of the wait. A released model is withdrawn and refuses new requests as model_not_selected; in-flight requests finish before eviction.
- Head 285-288 add invariant 10. Head 300-304 add a failure mode: an enabled_models edit applies only on restart or a committed switch.

Security relevance: this is availability/residency policy (A-018, TB-012/T-059 add-on hold interplay; T-029 idle). The described behavior preserves retirement of in-flight work and keeps the add-on hold authoritative. It grants no new authorization, attestation, encryption or data-exposure path. Recovery loads only operator-selected models and loosens no memory gate. No regression is identified from the docs.

Questions for integration (unverified because code is absent):
1. Does enterAddonHold actually cancel recovery attempts in ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift, so no model loads beside VMs (T-059 model-load fence)?
2. Does withdrawal of a released adoption refuse new requests before eviction?
3. Does isProtectedFromRecoveryEviction correctly exclude held and in-flight slots?
4. Do coordinator-driven controls avoid an eviction/reload loop between recovery and Autopilot operations?
